ACF/ESS depend on the observable, sample budget, stationarity and estimator conventions; no single ESS universally characterizes a chain. Do not use rank-transformed bulk ESS directly as an estimator of the raw-scale mean’s Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE). A library returning ESS=N for a constant observable is not evidence of good mixing. Conditions and pitfalls Detailed balance alone does not establish irreducibility or aperiodicity. Multimodality, correlations and boundaries can slow mixing. High acceptance can simply reflect tiny moves. Thinning is not a general way to increase information for a fixed computational budget. Chains trapped in different modes can reveal a between-chain discrepancy, while chains all trapped in one mode can have R-hat near one despite a completely unexplored mode. Check known CDFs, mode occupancy and transitions alongside apparently favorable R-hat/ESS. Reflection-induced mode changes alone do not establish within-mode exploration. Passing a test that intentionally reproduces poor mixing or a diagnostic blind spot does not mean estimation succeeded in that scenario. Fixed-input thresholds are acceptance criteria for this small comparison, not finite-run guarantees, diagnostic false-positive rates or reliability for every seed and target. The local Gaussian random-walk MH used here is theoretically irreducible. Failure to leave a mode in a finite run is not described as a permanently nonergodic algorithm. What to check Check means, variances and quantiles for known targets, including asymmetric proposals and rejections. For multimodal cases report between-chain comparisons, autocorrelations, effective sample sizes and uncertainty; visually flat traces alone are not proof of convergence.
